claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; changes
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this specific Purview DLP integration for Intune-protected mobile apps.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "mobile apps" "Intune" DLP policy. Opened DLP overview, Intune protection overview and collection policy reference; results describe existing mobile MAM or Windows Edge, not this integration.

claims.claim: The collection policy reference lists Devices, Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI, Unmanaged cloud apps and Adaptive app scopes.
claims.quote: The following data sources are supported: ... Devices ... Copilot experiences ... Enterprise AI ... Unmanaged cloud apps ... Adaptive app scopes

claims.claim: The collection policy reference does not list a mobile managed-app data source.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "mobile apps" "Intune" DLP policy. Opened collection policy reference: Devices is Windows; other sources are Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI, Unmanaged cloud apps and Adaptive app scopes; no managed mobile app source.

claims.claim: The DLP overview's location list has no Intune-managed mobile app entry.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview DLP Intune mobile apps New-DlpCompliancePolicy Microsoft Graph policy location MAM. Opened and searched DLP overview for Intune, mobile and MAM; none appears in its locations. Devices are Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS.

claims.claim: The Intune route to clipboard controls is Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS > Data protection.
claims.quote: Select Apps > Protection. ... Select Create policy and select either iOS/iPadOS or Android. ... Click Next to display the Data protection page. ... including cut, copy, paste, and save-as restrictions.
claims.fix: Complete the route as 'Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS > Basics > Apps > Data protection > Restrict cut, copy and paste between other apps'. The Basics fields and app targeting are pass-through or scope selections, not blockers. The final setting label is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/app-management/protection/ref-settings-ios.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Intune's Restrict cut, copy and paste between other apps setting controls clipboard sharing for protected apps.
claims.quote: Restrict cut, copy and paste between other apps | Specify when cut, copy, and paste actions can be used with this app.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/deviceAppManagement/iosManagedAppProtections creates an iOS policy whose allowedOutboundClipboardSharingLevel sets clipboard sharing.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceAppManagement/iosManagedAppProtections ... allowedOutboundClipboardSharingLevel ... The level to which the clipboard may be shared between apps on the managed device.

claims.claim: The existing Intune control is not documented as configuring the new Purview capability, or as being read or overridden by it.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Intune mobile DLP clipboard no policy configured default enforcement identity evaluation precedence. Opened Intune create-policy, overview, iOS settings and Purview Graph overview; no text connects the clipboard setting to this integration.

claims.claim: Collection policies filter which events Purview ingests from supported data sources.
claims.quote: They let you filter which events from both untrusted and trusted sources are ingested into Purview.

claims.claim: Collection policies provide discovery rather than enforcement, so a collection policy alone does not block an action.
claims.quote: Collection Policies are designed to streamline discovery of relevant information rather than to apply enforcement on that information.

claims.claim: Collection policies are at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, select Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the policy list. Qualify the row note with 'This route opens the collection policy list; use + Create policy to configure a policy, then + Add activities to choose activities to detect', as documented at the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/collection-policies-create-deploy-policy.

claims.claim: No API or cmdlet for creating or changing these event collection policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview collection policies create update API PowerShell New collection policy; "collection policies" "PowerShell" event collection filtering. Opened collection create/deploy and Graph security overview. Results show UI creation, scope evaluation or unrelated Data Map metadata RBAC.
